# Security Policy

## Supported versions

Security issues are considered for the latest stable release of Kick Stream Tweaks only. The current version is 1.3.1. Please update to the latest release before reporting an issue.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Do not disclose suspected security vulnerabilities in public GitHub Issues, Discussions, pull requests, or comments.

If GitHub’s private vulnerability reporting is enabled for this repository, submit a private report through [Security Advisories](https://github.com/ebayybe/kick-stream-tweaks/security/advisories). If it is unavailable, use [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/ebayybe/kick-stream-tweaks/issues) only to request a private contact method. Do not include vulnerability details in a public issue.

Please include the affected script version, browser and userscript manager versions, a clear impact description, and reproduction steps. Use synthetic data and a minimal proof of concept where possible.

Never include passwords, session cookies, access tokens, private account information, or unredacted personal data. Allow time for investigation and a fix before public disclosure. Reports are handled on a best-effort basis; no response or fix timeline is guaranteed.

## Scope and safe testing

This policy covers security issues caused by Kick Stream Tweaks itself, such as unexpected script behavior, unsafe handling of settings stored in the browser, or unintended interactions with the Kick player.

Test only accounts, systems, and data that you own or are explicitly authorized to use. Do not probe or attack Kick.com, its infrastructure, GitHub, browsers, userscript managers, or other third-party services. Report issues in those services to their respective maintainers.

For ordinary bugs and feature requests, use [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/ebayybe/kick-stream-tweaks/issues).
